## Why the three ORB columns are not the same size

All three are XCDR1 and payload only — CORBA CDR *is* XCDR1, CORBA 3.3 part 2 §9.3 — and all three are offered the same cases, so the difference between them is worth the arithmetic. It is two things, and only the second is about the ORBs:

| column | cases with a CORBA form | orders it writes | cells offered | cells with bytes | cases it refused |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `omniorb` | 302 | 2 | 604 | 512 | 46 |
| `tao` | 271 | 1 | 271 | 246 | 25 |
| `jacorb` | 271 | 1 | 271 | 240 | 31 |

The `cells offered` column is `cases with a CORBA form` times `orders it writes`, and it is where the factor of two lives: `ACE_OutputCDR::write_4` swaps only when libACE was built with `ACE_ENABLE_SWAP_ON_WRITE` and this build was not, and `org.jacorb.orb.CDROutputStream` has no `setLittleEndian` at all — only `CDRInputStream` does. Neither is a result; both are recorded once here and cited by every `one order` cell.

What the last column holds is the part that is a result, and [`write.md`](write.md) carries each refusal with the ORB's own sentence. Two of them belong to every ORB and to none of them: `primitive-char-above-latin1` and `primitive-wchar-above-bmp` are refused by this project's **fill**, before any ORB front end runs, because the OMG IDL-to-C++ and IDL-to-Java mappings give `char` and `wchar` no room for the value.

33365 of the 35896 rows that carry bytes come from a product such a machine can install; 2531 do not. The second number is not a smaller matrix — it is the same matrix with the rows named, one system at a time, below.

### `opendds` — OpenDDS 3.34.0 / ACE 6.5.24

The only IDL front end of the five whose `map` compiles, and the only DDS implementation here with CORBA/TAO lineage: `opendds_idl --idl-version 4` plus `tao_idl -Sa -St` produces the classic C++ mapping, so `wireprobe-opendds` takes the same CORBA C++ fill the omniORB and TAO probes take. `OpenDDS::DCPS::Serializer`, whose `Encoding` carries both the version and the byte order, so one build answers all four combinations. Its 504 refusals are the CORBA C++ fill's and are worded as the probe's, not the vendor's: OpenDDS's own front end parses `map`, and `wireprobe-fill`'s CORBA C++ output has no form for one.

- 1168 of 4210 rows carry bytes.
- Regenerated by `tools/interop-results/record.sh --vendors opendds`.
- Reachable without a licensed toolchain: yes.

### `hdds` — HDDS, hddsgen 1.2.0

The second pure-Rust DDS implementation. `hddsgen gen rust` generates the type and its own `encode_*` methods; `wireprobe-hdds` compiles that output unedited against the declaration shim in `tools/wireprobe/hdds-shim/`, because the published `hdds` crate does not carry the trait surface the generated code implements. Structural limits, each measured: no big-endian encoder, no parameter-list encoder — one framing per encoding version, whatever the type's extensibility says — and a front end that accepts all corpus cases it parses while its serialiser frames `@appendable` and `@mutable` types as `@final`, with no DHEADER and no EMHEADER. `Dialect::Hdds` carries those departures, opt-in, and reproduces every recorded row.

- 326 of 4210 rows carry bytes.
- Regenerated by `tools/interop-results/record.sh --vendors hdds`.
- Reachable without a licensed toolchain: yes.

### `opensplice` — OpenSplice Community Edition 6.9 (OSPL_V6_9_210323OSS_RELEASE)

`idlpp -S -l cpp` (standalone C++, the CORBA C++ mapping) plus `DDS::OpenSplice::CdrTypeSupport::serialize`. Its IDL is OMG IDL 3.5: no annotation parses, keys are `#pragma keylist`, so `wireprobe-opensplice` rewrites a case only where every construct means the same XCDR1 bytes in that IDL and refuses the rest by name — `@mutable`, `@optional`, `@external`, `@must_understand`, `@value`, an enum `@bit_bound` below 32, `bitmask`, `bitset`, `map`, and a union as the topic type. `idlpp` itself refuses `wchar`, `wstring`, `fixed`, struct inheritance, empty structs, `octet` and `int8`/`uint8` discriminators and struct-typed key members. Four cases are accepted by `idlpp` and its own generated C++ does not compile: the three recursive types (forward-declared structs are defined twice), a type named `static`, and an `unsigned long long` case label above the signed range.

- 191 of 4210 rows carry bytes.
- Regenerated by `tools/interop-results/record.sh --vendors opensplice`.
- Reachable without a licensed toolchain: yes.

### `omniorb` — omniORB 4.3.3

`omniidl -bcxx` plus `cdrMemoryStream`. The only one of the three that writes both byte orders, which is where the factor of two between this column and the other two comes from and not from anything it accepts that they do not. It refuses ten cases: the eight `union-discriminator-{octet,int8,uint8,wchar}` (J9), where it answers `Syntax error in union declaration` and then `Cannot create an instance of union 'Choice' inside its own definition`, which is a remark about its own recovery and not about the case; and the two the fill refuses before any ORB sees them.

- 512 of 4210 rows carry bytes.
- Regenerated by `tools/interop-results/record.sh --orbs`.
- Reachable without a licensed toolchain: no.

### `tao` — TAO 2.5.24

`tao_idl -as` plus `TAO_OutputCDR`. Writes little endian only: `ACE_OutputCDR::write_4` swaps only when libACE was built with `ACE_ENABLE_SWAP_ON_WRITE`, and this build was not. It refuses omniORB's ten and ten more, all `fixed<P,S>` — and it refuses them **at exit status 0**: `Error - tao_idl: "gen.idl", line L: fixed data types are not supported`, 294 lines over the ten cases, on a run that reports success. The probe catches it because `genC.cpp` is not there afterwards, which is the only reason this column is not ten cases of empty bytes. A severity in this front end's output is not a claim its exit status backs.

- 246 of 4210 rows carry bytes.
- Regenerated by `tools/interop-results/record.sh --orbs`.
- Reachable without a licensed toolchain: no.

### `jacorb` — JacORB 3.9

`org.jacorb.idl.parser` plus `CDROutputStream`. Writes big endian only: `org.jacorb.orb.CDROutputStream` has no `setLittleEndian` — only `CDRInputStream` does. It refuses 24 cases, which is the most of the three, and 14 of them are two defects of its own rather than J9's discriminator question. **A union case label outside the signed range of its Java holder**: `Illegal case label <3735928559> for integral switch type int` for an `unsigned long` discriminator, the same for `unsigned long long`, `long long` treated as 32-bit, and `unsigned short` reaching `javac` as `Choice.java:33: error: incompatible types: possible lossy conversion from int to short` in JacORB's **own** generated code — eight cases. **A `default:` branch it can only give discriminator 0**: the generated `fraction(int _discriminator, double _x)` throws `BAD_OPERATION` for any other, so a sample selecting the default with an unlisted label has no JacORB form — six cases, `array-1d-union`, `sequence-union` and `union-with-default`.

- 240 of 4210 rows carry bytes.
- Regenerated by `tools/interop-results/record.sh --orbs`.
- Reachable without a licensed toolchain: no.
